item.title: Countable models of one-dimensional Peano continua
item.description: arXiv:2610.35875v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove that a one-dimensional Peano continuum $X$ admits a weak homotopy equivalence $X\to C$ to a countable space $C$ if and only if the wild set $\mathbf{w}(X)$ is countable.
item.dc:creator: Jeremy Brazas, Petar Pavesic

item.title: On families of copulas and quasi-copulas homeomorphic to the Hilbert cube and related results
item.description: arXiv:2610.35912v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Working with tools from infinite-dimensional topology and using measure-theoretic ideas we analyze numerous well-known fami\-lies of copu\-las and quasi-copulas from a topological perspective, prove that most of them are homeomorphic to the Hilbert cube $\mathcal{H}$ and hence have the Fixed Point as well as the Disjoint Cells property. Working with so-called $Z$-sets, we then study how large one set is within another. Doing so, in order to show that a set $A$ is small/topologically negligible within a compact metric space $(\Omega,m)$, we construct a homeomorphism $h: [0,1] \times \mathcal{H} \to \Omega$ mapping $\{0\} \times \mathcal{H}$ to $A$. The obtained results are to a certain extent surprising since various supposedly small families are topologically large.
item.dc:creator: Fabrizio Durante, Juan Fern\'andez S\'anchez, Wolfgang Trutschnig

item.title: Function spaces with compact-open topology need not be sober
item.description: arXiv:2610.36551v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We exhibit sober spaces $X$ and $Y$ such that the function space $[X \to Y]_K$ of continuous maps, equipped with the compact-open topology, is not sober; the codomain can be chosen to be the Sierpi\'nski space $S$. Our construction builds on Isbell's complete lattice $M$, whose Scott space $\Sigma M$ is non-sober. Let $H = Q(M)$ be the set of nonempty compact saturated subsets of $\Sigma M$, ordered by reverse inclusion. Since $H$ is well known to be a spatial frame, the space $X = \mathrm{pt}(H)$ is sober with $\mathcal{O}(X) \cong H$. The key technical result is that sobriety of the space $H$ would entail sobriety of the original Scott space $\Sigma M$. This contradicts Isbell's example, and the desired counterexample follows.
item.dc:creator: Bei Liu, Qingguo Li

item.title: On various notions of universally Baire sets and reflection of non-Baire property in Cantor sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.36265v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Universally Baire sets are a standard tool in modern set theory, where they are closely connected with forcing and absoluteness. In this paper we study universal Baireness instead as purely a regularity notion for subsets of Polish spaces. Our aim is not to develop the set-theoretic theory, but to place the notion on a systematic descriptive-set-theoretic footing and to clarify the several nonequivalent definitions that occur in the literature. A subset of a Polish space is called \emph{universally Baire} if all its continuous preimages possess the property of Baire. However, it is important to specify what the domain of these continuous functions can be. In fact, a plethora of definitions are used by various authors in the literature, the class of possible domains is sometimes the class of Polish spaces, compact metrizable spaces, all topological spaces, compact topological spaces, etc. We clarify this situation by demonstrating that the above four options are pairwise nonequivalent under the Continuum Hypothesis, we determine all the implications between these four notions that are provable in $ZFC$, and also show that all the notions used in the literature are equivalent to one of these four. Furthermore, we use Miller forcing to show that actually the cases of Polish and compact metrizable spaces are consistently equivalent. We show that numerous definitions using Borel isomorphisms, changes of topologies and Boolean algebras are all equivalent to the case of Polish domains. We present an argument that the notion using Polish domains is the natural dual to the notion of universally measurable sets. Finally, as a byproduct, we prove that the following statement is independent of $ZFC$: if a subset of a Polish space has the property of Baire relative to every nowhere dense Cantor subspace, then the subset has the property of Baire in the whole space.
item.dc:creator: M\'arton Elekes, M\'at\'e P\'alfy

item.title: Continuum-wise hyperbolicity is exactly the pseudo-Anosov dynamics with spine singularities
item.description: arXiv:2606.11943v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish a complete structural classification for cw$_F$-hyperbolic surface homeomorphisms. Specifically, we prove that a surface homeomorphism is cw$_F$-hyperbolic if, and only if, it is a pseudo-Anosov homeomorphism whose singularities consist exclusively of spines (1-prongs). Furthermore, we classify these systems up to topological conjugacy, showing that every such homeomorphism is conjugate to either an Anosov automorphism on the torus $\mathbb{T}^2$ or to a standard hyperelliptic quotient on $\mathbb{S}^2$ of a hyperbolic affine toral map. As a rigid consequence of this classification, we show that such dynamics are strictly obstructed on surfaces of genus greater than one, the Klein bottle, and the projective plane.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Arruda, Bernardo Carvalho, Piotr Oprocha, Alberto Sarmiento

item.title: Compactifications of Abelian Group Bundles and a Topological Halmos--von Neumann-type Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2608.28335v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The topological Halmos--von Neumann theorem is a fundamental result of topological dynamics that completely classifies continuous actions of abelian topological groups which are ergodic and have discrete spectrum. It rests on a correspondence between such actions (up to the choice of a distinguished point), compactifications of the acting group and subgroups of its dual group. We generalize both the classical statement and the underlying categorical equivalences to the framework of open group bundles over locally compact base spaces. As a byproduct, we establish a Pontryagin-type duality between \'etale Hausdorff abelian group bundles and open proper Hausdorff abelian group bundles, extending the classical duality between discrete and compact abelian groups.
item.dc:creator: Dustin Anglewitz, Patrick Hermle, Henrik Kreidler
